result.summary: Henry Ingram, the landlord, approved by email (event 009) the tenant's request to replace the broken LG washing machine with one of their own and keep it when they move out. I recorded that approval. The agency had already told the tenant (event 010), and the tenant's brother is taking the old machine to the tip himself. That means no contractor is needed and no removal charge is expected. I emailed the landlord to say so and closed the ticket.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 009 says 'Yes this is fine', in reply to the agency email in event 005. That email had the correct address and asked two things: whether the tenant can replace the machine with their own and keep it, and whether the landlord will cover any removal charge. classify_reply rated it an approval at 1.0, with a 0.88 chance of being unconditional and autonomy 'auto'. In event 010 the tenant was told and said their brother will take the old machine away. All that was left was to record the approval, update the property record, tell the paying party there's no charge expected, and close the ticket.

alternatives_considered.option: Move to provider selection or assign a contractor
alternatives_considered.why_not: The tenant is supplying and fitting their own machine and getting rid of the old one, so there's nothing for a contractor to do.

alternatives_considered.option: Escalate because of the address mismatch in the event 004 call note
alternatives_considered.why_not: The call note gives the address as Flat 18, 128 Meadow Row, which looks like a note-taking slip. The landlord approved by replying to the email in event 005, which had the correct address. The mismatch doesn't change the decision.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep open in closeout and wait for the tenant to confirm the new machine is in
alternatives_considered.why_not: No agency work or landlord cost is left. The tenant has already thanked us, so chasing them would just add noise.
They were fully updated on the call in event 010.

checks_performed: Pending approval 36: the landlord's reply was clear and had no conditions (classify_reply: intent approve, autonomy auto)
Address: the approval email (event 005) matches the property. The event 004 call note gives a different address.
Cost: no removal charge expected because the tenant is disposing of the old machine. The landlord had agreed to cover around £24.37–30 if one arose.
No open holds, no human-queue items, no attachments, no safety risk
assumptions: 'Riverside Solutions' in event 010 and 'Northbridge Lettings' are the same agency under different trading names
The wrong address in the event 004 call note is a recording error
